questions.prompt: An App Service app needs more memory per worker and a higher-tier feature. Which operation addresses these requirements?

options.text: Scale up the App Service plan to a suitable SKU.
options.explanation: Scale up changes worker resources and tier features.

options.text: Only increase worker count with the existing SKU.
options.explanation: Scale out adds workers but does not increase memory per worker or unlock higher-tier features.
A slot consumes the existing plan capacity.

options.text: Only set a larger maximum autoscale count.
options.explanation: A count limit does not change the worker SKU.

questions.prompt: A Standard App Service plan normally runs two instances. It must run four instances from 08:00 to 18:00 every Monday through Friday, using UTC, and two at other times regardless of CPU demand. Which Azure Monitor autoscale configuration implements this recurring capacity schedule?

options.text: Use weekday 08:00 profiles fixed at four instances and weekday 18:00 profiles fixed at two instances.
options.explanation: Recurring profiles switch capacity at the specified times. Setting each profile minimum, default, and maximum to its required count fixes four during the workday and two after the evening switch, including the weekend.

options.text: Use weekday 08:00 profiles fixed at two instances and weekday 18:00 profiles fixed at four instances.
options.explanation: These profiles reverse the required capacity: two during the workday and four overnight.

options.text: Use daily 08:00 profiles fixed at four instances and daily 18:00 profiles fixed at two instances.
options.explanation: Daily recurrence also allocates four instances during weekend days, when the requirement is two.

options.text: Use weekday 08:00 profiles fixed at four instances and weekday 18:00 profiles also fixed at four instances.
options.explanation: The evening profile does not restore two instances; it retains four outside the required workday.

questions.prompt: A Premium v3 web app uses App Service automatic HTTP scaling. Five always-ready instances are serving requests, and one additional prewarmed instance is allocated as a buffer. The app also has a staging slot used for load testing. Which TWO statements are correct about cost and scaling support? Select two individual statements.

options.text: The allocated prewarmed instance is billable while it is held as a buffer.
options.explanation: Allocated prewarmed instances are billed even before they serve application requests; the scenario confirms that this buffer exists.

options.text: The staging-slot traffic is unsupported as input for this automatic scaling feature.
options.explanation: Automatic HTTP scaling does not support deployment-slot traffic, so that load test cannot be treated as supported production scaling input.

options.text: The prewarmed instance becomes billable only after it starts serving application requests.
options.explanation: Billing begins when the prewarmed instance is allocated, not when it becomes an active request-serving worker.

options.text: The staging slot has the same supported automatic HTTP scaling behavior as the production app.
options.explanation: The feature excludes deployment-slot traffic; production-app support does not extend it to the slot.
